well-being = a state of being healthy, comfortable and content, not only free from illness
quality of life = how good or bad a person’s life feels in health, comfort and opportunity
life expectancy = the average number of years a person in a group is expected to live
public health = organised efforts to protect and improve the health of a whole population
health literacy = the ability to find, understand and use information to make health decisions
health inequality = unfair differences in health between social or economic groups
preventive care = medical services that stop illness before it starts or catches it early
risk factor = something that raises the chance of developing a disease
underlying condition = an existing long-term illness that makes other problems more serious
immune system = the body’s defences against infection
health promotion = activity that encourages people to live in ways that protect their health
screening programme = organised tests offered to a group to find disease early
early detection = finding a disease at a stage when treatment works better
preventable disease = an illness that vaccination, hygiene or lifestyle change can stop
universal healthcare = a system in which everyone can get medical care, usually paid from taxes
private healthcare = medical care paid for by the patient or a private insurer, not the state
medical ethics = moral rules that guide doctors, such as doing no harm and respecting choice
informed consent = agreement to treatment after the risks and benefits have been explained
patient confidentiality = the duty to keep a patient’s medical information private
chronic illness = a disease that lasts a long time and often cannot be fully cured
